correctness.rationale: The star/top theorem implies every adjacent pair belongs to exactly two maximal cliques whose common intersection is a (q+1)-vertex pencil. The fixed-(k-2)-flat count gives an empty-label star for any support of at most three vertices because [4]_q>3(q+1). Each nonpencil triangle realizes all eight labels; each pencil triangle fails a two-positive trace. Unique maximal clique containment of a nonpencil triple prohibits four-point shattering. Every depth-four online tree would have a double-positive depth-two branch with at most two concepts. Incidence and projective collinearity counts give the Gaussian coefficients and purity. Direct maximal-clique graph enumeration verifies full triple counts at (q,n,k)=(2,4,2),(3,4,2), all four-supports in the first case, and sampled higher instances.

evidence: The full published maximal-line-graph-clique theorem proves an online upper bound of three for all simple line graphs and a complete polynomial only for complete-graph line graphs. Grassmann graph edges belong to two maximal cliques of cardinality at least seven, whereas in a simple line graph any two distinct maximal cliques containing an edge have one triangular clique of size three; therefore the general line-graph theorem does not apply to these Grassmann graphs.

The full published maximal intersecting edge-family result concerns edges of complete graphs (the rank-two set-valued Johnson case), not q-ary subspaces. The published affine-flat and flag results use different concept families.
